attributes.description: An independent contemporary art centre and exhibition space in Douala.
attributes.founded: 1991, by Princess Marilyn Douala Manga Bell and the art historian Didier Schaub.
attributes.main_project: The SUD Salon Urbain de Douala triennial of public art.
attributes.landmark: La Nouvelle Liberté by Joseph-Francis Sumégné, commissioned in 1996.

source.citation: Wikipedia, SUD Salon Urbain de Douala (CC BY-SA 4.0), C& magazine, the Goethe-Institut, and doual'art's SUD2017 page. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.description: A triennial festival of public art and contemporary art in Douala, organised by doual'art.
attributes.editions: The first was in December 2007, the second in December 2010, the third in 2013 on the theme Douala Métamorphoses, and the fourth in 2017 on the theme La place de l'Humain, dedicated to youth.
attributes.output: Performances, installations and permanent public artworks. Counts differ: one source says more than 80 works and events, another says around sixty works.
attributes.permanent_works: Include L'Arbre à Palabres by Frédéric Keiff and Nje Mo Ye by Koko Komégné.
attributes.impact: Douala has taken on public art projects, with monuments unveiled or renovated, thanks to SUD.

source.citation: Wikipedia, List of public art in Douala (CC BY-SA 4.0), Erika Nimis in Ciel Variable, and Kupi. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.year: Commissioned in 1996 by doual'art. It was inaugurated in the framework of SUD2007.
attributes.description: A permanent monumental sculpture in recycled material, about 12 metres high with a wingspan of 5 metres.
attributes.place: The Deïdo traffic circle in Douala.
attributes.meaning: Regarded as the unofficial symbol of the city.

source.citation: Wikipedia, List of Cameroonian artists (CC BY-SA 4.0), Wikipedia on SUD, and an Artpaper overview. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.names: Joseph-Francis Sumégné (born 1951), Pascale Marthine Tayou (born 1967), Barthélémy Toguo (born 1967), Hervé Yamguen (born 1971), Goddy Leye, Salifou Lindou, Koko Komégné, Boris Nzebo and others.
attributes.public_art_examples: Pascale Marthine Tayou made a permanent totem of enamel pots for SUD 2010 and Madiba Square for SUD 2013.
